title: OO Agents: Native Python Object-Oriented Agents (NOOA)
path: agents/harness/[Paper] OO Agents Native Python Object-Oriented Agents (NOOA).md
summary: NVIDIA's NOOA reframes an agent as a plain Python object: methods are the actions the model can take, fields are its state, docstrings are prompts, and type annotations are contracts — a method whose body is `...` becomes an LLM-driven agentic loop while normal method bodies stay deterministic Python, so agent behavior can be tested, traced, refactored, and versioned like ordinary software. Argues (inspired by PyTorch's "powerful runtime, simple Python surface") for reusing mature language abstractions instead of DSLs/graphs, and identifies six model-facing capabilities it is first to combine on one surface: typed I/O, pass-by-reference over live objects, code-as-action, programmable loop engineering, explicit object state, and model-callable harness APIs for context/events. Surveys fourteen frameworks/harnesses (LangGraph, Deep Agents, Microsoft Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, PydanticAI, smolagents, Claude Agent SDK, …) scored on those six axes, and evaluates the interface on SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, and ARC-AGI-3.

Sharply improves accuracy on math, symbolic, and algorithmic benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K) by decoupling 'decompose the problem' (LLM) from 'compute the answer' (interpreter).
